title: Pardons Aviem Sella
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Aviem Sella as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s pardon list includes Aviem Sella under January 19, 2021, although this record is dated May 24, 2018. The DOJ table lists the District of Columbia, no sentence, and offenses involving conspiracy to gather or deliver national-defense information and receiving classified information as a foreign agent.
description_long: The Justice Department’s pardon list identifies Aviem Sella in its January 19, 2021 section, while the supplied event record carries a May 24, 2018 date. The DOJ entry places the case in the District of Columbia and lists no sentence. It describes two counts of conspiracy to gather or deliver national-defense information and a violation involving receipt or possession of classified information by a foreign agent. Those labels establish the subject of the federal case as represented in the official clemency table, but do not say whether Sella was convicted, what conduct was proved, or what legal proceedings preceded the pardon. The mismatch in the date is material, and the available entry does not reproduce the pardon warrant or explain the decision. The date and case history should be resolved before this can be presented as a complete account.
notes: The linked DOJ pardon list places Sella in the January 19, 2021 group, conflicting with the input date May 24, 2018. It lists espionage-related offenses and no sentence but does not establish the case disposition or conduct. Proposed correction: verify the event date against the pardon instrument; do not silently replace the original date.

title: Pardons Chalmer Lee Williams
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Chalmer Lee Williams as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department lists Chalmer Lee Williams among the July 29, 2019 pardon recipients. His Eastern District of Kentucky case involved conspiracy to steal firearms and other goods from interstate shipments, with a four-month prison sentence and three years of supervised release. The list does not describe the specific shipments or Williams’s role.
description_long: Donald Trump’s July 29, 2019 clemency list includes Chalmer Lee Williams, whose case was prosecuted in the Eastern District of Kentucky. The Justice Department records a sentence of four months in prison and three years of supervised release, imposed in 1995. The listed offenses were conspiracy to steal firearms and other goods as part of an interstate shipment, theft from an interstate shipment, and theft of firearms shipped in interstate commerce. These details identify the federal case and the original punishment, but the DOJ table does not describe the shipment, the number or value of firearms, Williams’s specific role, or any consequences to victims. It also does not explain why the president selected the case or state the pardon’s terms. A case-level record or contemporary report is needed to add those facts without turning the offense labels into an invented narrative.
notes: The linked DOJ pardon list confirms the July 29, 2019 clemency entry, Eastern District of Kentucky, sentence, and interstate-shipment/firearm offenses. It does not detail the conduct, Williams’s role, victims, or the reason for clemency.

title: Pardons Lynn Wade Barney
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Lynn Wade Barney as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department lists Lynn Wade Barney in its January 13, 2021 pardon group. The District of Utah case involved possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon; the recorded sentence was 35 months in prison and three years of supervised release.
description_long: Lynn Wade Barney appears in the Justice Department’s January 13, 2021 list of pardons granted by Donald Trump. The DOJ table places his case in the District of Utah and identifies the offense as possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. It records a sentence of 35 months’ imprisonment and three years of supervised release, imposed in 2005. This provides the conviction category and original punishment, but not the circumstances of the firearm possession, how the offense came to investigators’ attention, or any case-specific mitigating information. The list also does not state why Trump selected Barney for a pardon or reproduce the warrant’s scope. Those missing facts matter to an account of the individual clemency decision, especially because the offense label alone does not explain the conduct or the rationale.
notes: The linked DOJ pardon list provides the date group, district, offense, and sentence, but not the underlying conduct, case circumstances, pardon terms, or a documented rationale.

title: Pardons Alfonso Antonio Costa
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Alfonso Antonio Costa as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s December 22, 2020 pardon list names Alfonso Antonio Costa, convicted of health care fraud in the Western District of Pennsylvania. It records three years’ probation, one year of home confinement, 100 hours of community service, a $250,000 fine, and $44,579.47 in restitution.
description_long: The Justice Department lists Alfonso Antonio Costa among the December 22, 2020 pardons. His case was in the Western District of Pennsylvania, where he was convicted of health care fraud. The sentence recorded by DOJ was three years’ probation, conditioned on one year of home confinement and 100 hours of community service, along with a $250,000 fine and $44,579.47 in restitution. Those figures describe the penalties attached to the conviction before clemency. The list does not explain what claims or billing conduct formed the fraud, identify affected patients or programs, or say how the restitution figure was calculated. It also gives no reason for the pardon and does not reproduce its legal terms. A case-specific account would be needed to explain Costa’s conduct and the pardon’s practical effect; the clemency table alone establishes the conviction category, sentence, and grant.
notes: The linked DOJ pardon list confirms Costa’s offense, district, original sentence and financial penalties, and the December 22, 2020 grant group. It does not describe the underlying health-care fraud or the pardon rationale/terms.

title: Pardons Gary Mark Brugman
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Gary Mark Brugman as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s December 23, 2020 pardon list includes Gary Mark Brugman, whose Western District of Texas case resulted in 27 months in prison and two years of supervised release for deprivation of rights under color of law. The table does not explain the conduct behind the offense.
description_long: Gary Mark Brugman appears in the Justice Department’s December 23, 2020 pardon list. The official table identifies his case as one in the Western District of Texas and records a 27-month prison sentence followed by two years of supervised release. It names the offense as deprivation of rights under color of law, with the sentence imposed in 2003. That label indicates a federal civil-rights offense but does not identify Brugman’s role, whose rights were affected, or what actions led to the conviction. The DOJ list confirms that Trump granted a pardon but supplies no case narrative or explanation for selecting Brugman. Without the judgment, pardon warrant, or event-specific reporting, it would be misleading to supply the underlying conduct or claim a particular motive. The available record supports the grant and sentence, while leaving the most important case details unresolved.
